setlist.title: It's All Over Now, Baby Blue

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Hey Jude** (2 reviews): Brent played Hey Jude with fierce intensity, according to the reviewer; Reviewer says he missed every note of Hey Jude [21][27]
- **Candyman** (1 review): Reviewer singles out Candyman as worth the download on its own [18]
- **I Know You Rider** (1 review): Reviewer calls the China Cat/Rider and Ship of Fools strong, killer performances [18]
- **Dear Mr. Fantasy** (1 other source): Soundboard has a cut of about 2.6 seconds around 21 seconds in, patched from the audience recording [2]
- **Truckin'** (1 review): Truckin' is described as especially strong, following the Hey Jude [21]
- **Just A Little Light** (1 review): Attendee vaguely remembers Just a Little Light as the one moment that stuck from the night [19]

## Setlist highlights

- **Just A Little Thought**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [29]

## The recordings

- **gd1990-04-01.mtx.hansokolow.97203.flac16** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 22 songs; 166 min; rated 5/5 by 2 [1]
- **gd1990-04-01.matrix.sirmick.35168.sbeok.flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 22 songs; 164 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [2]. Said about its sound: Audience source ran about 1.35% slow and was corrected; a 2.6-second soundboard cut in Dear Mr. Fantasy was patched from the audience tape [2]
- **gd1990-04-01.158174.ultramatrix.miller.flac2496**: soundboard; 22 songs; 162 min [4]
- **gd90-04-01.aud.gardner.3458.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 23 songs; 170 min; rated 4.5/5 by 8 [5]. Said about its sound: Audience tape has adequate levels, clear strong vocals, and an energized crowd; better than most Omni audience recordings [23]
- **gd90-04-01.sbd.gorinsky.8512.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 22 songs; 157 min; rated 4.4/5 by 15 [8]. Said about its sound: Reviewer judges this the best-sounding recording of the three-show Atlanta run, rating the sound highly; performance very tight [21]

## Around the show

- Attendee, at his second Dead show, circled the Omni several times before finding his seat; Rex Foundation table staff asked if he was lost [17]
- The tour ended in Atlanta, with the band at a peak; first set ran ten songs, ending with To Lay Me Down [22]
- Crowd outside the Omni was large, tickets scarce; the reviewer eventually bought a $100 ticket from a scalper after waiting with finger raised [25]
- Parking lot scene clashed with irritated office workers, and bumper stickers were passed around outside the CNN building [26]
- The Omni had a cavernous ceiling reminiscent of H.R. Giger's art; the building has since been torn down [26]
- Counterfeit tickets were around; a fan shared a psychedelic liquid from a leather waterskin and watched the band seem to turn into cartoon bears [27]
- Three songs from this night appeared on the album Without a Net; reviewer calls it among the best-sounding Dead recordings [22]
- Reviewer places the show within spring 1990, saying the band was at its best in years [23]
- This run felt less relaxed than the previous year's [26]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1990-04-01.mtx.hansokolow.97203.flac16**: transferred by hansokolow; source: matrix of SBD: shnid=87809 and AUD: shnid=3458 by hansokolow using ProTools [1]
- **gd1990-04-01.matrix.sirmick.35168.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by SirMick; source: Matrix by Sir Mick [2]. Also: Matrix of a 24-track soundboard mixdown with an audience tape recorded with Nakamichi 300/CP4 and Sennheiser 441 microphones, via Sony D10 Pro [2]
- **gd1990-04-01.158174.ultramatrix.miller.flac2496**: taped by Recorded by Don Pearson and Dan Healy; transferred by All Transfers and Mastering by Charlie Miller  September 18, 2022; source: Ultramatrix SBD > Cassette Master (TDK SA-X90) [4]. Also: Ultramatrix recorded by Don Pearson and Dan Healy, with several masters used to complete the show; 24-bit/96k version [4]
- **gd90-04-01.aud.gardner.3458.sbeok.shnf**: source: aud MC> DAT> CD-R [5]. Also: Reviewer notes this audience source differs slightly from another circulating source and was unexpected in the archive [24]
- **gd90-04-01.sbd.gorinsky.8512.sbeok.shnf**: source: 24 track SBD MR>Healy 2 track Mixdown>C>DAT>CDR [8]

facts.lineage: The Master Cassettes were played back with Azimuth adjustment and Dolby B decoding on a Nakamichi CD1 into a Korg MR1000 at DSF 1 bit 5.6MHz. Subsequent conversion to 24/96 AIFF done via Korg Audiogate software. Redbook CDR standard 16/44.1 files were created using Bias Peak, Izotope Ozone's MBIT+ (for all dithering), and Weiss Saracon SRC (all sample rate conversions).
facts.source: 2 Nakamichi CM300s/ CP4's  w/1 Nakamichi CM300/CP2> Nakamichi 550 w/Maxell XLIIS90 cassette masters. Dolby B was used on the Master Cassettes. OTS 8 foot stand (sec. 128 Row DD Seat 3)
